subtopics.title: The Tangle of Factors That Hold Development Back

questions.question: Angola pumping oil while most Angolans stay poor, against Botswana turning diamonds into schools and clinics, best illustrates:
options: The resource curse — mineral wealth captured by a narrow elite blocks development, so outcomes depend on what a country does with its resources, not the resources themselves
That oil is less valuable than diamonds
That landlocked countries cannot develop
That resources guarantee development everywhere

questions.question: Why is unreliable energy supply a development factor rather than a mere inconvenience?
options: Because electricity prices set the exchange rate
Because without dependable power there are no factory shifts, vaccine fridges, irrigation pumps or evening study — and blackouts drain jobs and deter investment
Because energy is the only factor that matters
Because power stations employ most of the workforce

questions.question: Colonial railways were typically built:
options: To connect every town to its neighbours
To circle the coastline
From mine to harbour rather than from town to town, serving extraction instead of local development
To follow older trade routes exactly

questions.question: The word that unlocks questions on the causes of underdevelopment is:
options: Isolated
Temporary
Identical
Interrelated — each factor pulls on the others, so answers must trace the chain rather than one link

questions.question: The apartheid spatial legacy still shapes development because:
options: Forced removals and the homeland system settled millions far from work on poor land with thin services, and that geography outlives the laws that drew it
The old laws are still in force
Cities have stopped growing since 1994
The former homelands hold most of the country's industry

questions.question: South Africa's core inequality and unemployment figures are approximately:
options: Gini 0,30 and unemployment of 10 per cent
A Gini near 0,63 and unemployment above thirty per cent, rising past forty per cent among young people
A Gini near 0,90 and unemployment of 5 per cent
A Gini near 0,45 and unemployment of 15 per cent

questions.question: Vacancies for artisans and engineers existing alongside mass joblessness points to:
options: A shortage of ambition among work-seekers
Too many universities
A skills mismatch — high enrolment but weak outcomes leave the education pipeline leaking, which is the real bottleneck
An oversupply of qualified workers

questions.question: A balanced assessment of post-1994 development must hold together:
options: Only the gains in housing, water and electricity
Only the failures of maintenance and unemployment
Neither gains nor failures, since data is unreliable
Both the enormous expansion of services and grants AND the stubborn unemployment, inequality and institutional strain — both halves are true at once

subtopics.title: Community-Based Development: Rural and Urban Approaches

questions.question: The golden rule of community-based development is:
options: People maintain what is theirs — participation and ownership keep a project alive after the funders leave
Big projects always beat small ones
Technology should be as advanced as possible
Outside experts must make the final decisions

questions.question: The Wupperthal rooibos cooperatives in the Cederberg demonstrate that:
options: Rooibos only grows on large commercial farms
Small farmers who pool, process and market their harvest jointly keep profits in the valley and reach prices no lone grower could negotiate
Cooperatives always fail without state grants
Tea farming needs no local knowledge

questions.question: Warwick Junction in Durban became a productive precinct because:
options: The street traders were relocated to the city edge
Trading was banned near the interchange
Planners designed shelters, storage and cooking facilities WITH the traders around their actual daily trade
A shopping mall replaced the informal market

questions.question: Upgrading informal settlements in place is preferred to relocation because:
options: It is always cheaper for the municipality
Relocation buildings are poorly constructed
New land is impossible to find
Relocation severs the job links and social networks that keep poor households alive, while in-place upgrading keeps them intact

questions.question: The Olifants River case shows that:
options: A century of mining can leave a river acidic and metal-laden, delivering the environmental bill long after the profits were spent
Rivers recover quickly from mining pollution
Coal mining has no effect on water
Irrigation is impossible from any South African river

questions.question: Environmental damage is described as a loan against development because:
options: Banks finance most polluting industries
Eroded soil, polluted water and degraded land subtract from future production and wellbeing, so today's gain is repaid with interest tomorrow — mostly by the poor
Environmental fines are paid in instalments
Development always requires borrowing money

questions.question: Poverty itself degrades the environment when:
options: Poor households buy too many electrical appliances
Informal traders recycle waste
Households without electricity strip woodland for fuel and hungry herders overstock fragile veld — closing the circle back into deeper poverty
Rural families plant food gardens

questions.question: Named tools of sustainable development include:
options: Unlimited mining licences and voluntary clean-ups
Banning all new construction
Relocating settlements away from all rivers
Environmental impact assessments before major projects, binding mine rehabilitation duties, protected areas earning tourism income, and the shift from coal to sun and wind

questions.question: In the West Coast fishing family's story, the daughter leaving school to pack fish at the harbour is:
options: The education wire pulling tight — the resource shock converts into lost skills and lower future wages
The energy wire
The trade wire
Proof that schooling does not matter

questions.question: Selling whole fish cheaply and buying tinned fish back at four times the price is the family-scale version of:
options: The resource curse
Trade imbalance — exporting cheap raw products and importing expensive processed ones drains the capital development needs
Population growth
Service delivery failure

questions.question: The full-mark way to explain the causes of poverty is to:
options: Pick the single most important factor and ignore the rest
List the factors alphabetically without connections
Write the chain — show each wire pulling the next and use the word interrelated
Blame geography alone

questions.question: The distant-officials project fails most often because:
options: Nobody local can repair it or feels it is theirs, so the pump rusts once the officials leave
Trucks cannot reach rural areas
Big projects are always badly engineered
Communities refuse all outside help

questions.question: Working for Wetlands is a strong rural case because:
options: It builds dams across every river
Local crews heal eroded wetlands so catchments hold water again, while earning wages and portable skills — environment and livelihoods improved together
It relocates communities away from wetlands
It imports foreign specialists to do the work

questions.question: The Enkanini solar project outside Stellenbosch shows that:
options: Informal settlements cannot be electrified
Only the national grid can supply power
A community-run service can light shacks with pay-as-you-go solar years before the grid arrives
Solar power only works on formal housing

questions.question: The honest limitation to state about community-based development is:
options: It never produces any real benefits
It works only in rural areas
It makes state delivery unnecessary
It is powerful but small against national need — it complements state-scale delivery and cannot replace it

questions.question: The family burning its roof beams to stay warm stands for:
options: Development that consumes its own environment — a loan from tomorrow repaid with interest
Sensible use of spare building materials
The benefits of cheap energy
Poverty that has no environmental effects

questions.question: Overgrazed slopes washing into Eastern Cape dams as silt is a double loss because:
options: Silt improves water quality but damages pumps
The land loses its topsoil and the towns lose water storage capacity in the same motion
Dams are unaffected by sediment
Grazing has no link to erosion

questions.question: The environmental bill lands on the poor first because:
options: Wealthy areas produce no pollution
Environmental laws exempt poor areas
Shack settlements sit beside the dumps and drink from the polluted rivers, and their residents can least afford to move away
The poor are charged environmental taxes

questions.question: The one-sentence definition of sustainable development is:
options: Grow the economy as fast as possible
Stop all building and mining immediately
Let each generation solve only its own problems
Meet today's needs without stealing from your grandchildren's — development built to still be standing when they arrive
